tool_calling_support: llama.cpp ships a dedicated Bielik v3 chat template with full tool support (models/templates/Bielik-11B-v3.0-Instruct.jinja): ChatML framing, tools serialized inside <|function_list|> in the system turn, calls emitted as <tool_call>{"name","arguments"}</tool_call>, tool results fed back as <|function_output|> under a user turn. The server relies on the template embedded in the GGUF metadata (chat_template key); the launcher passes no --chat-template-file flag, so equivalence between the embedded template and the repo jinja file is unverified [uncertain]. llamacpp OpenAI-compat layer (/v1/chat/completions with tools) parses <tool_call> natively — this is the 'advanced template' path that stock ollama lacks. No tool-call parser gate was run against :8082 directly (gates targeted coopforge via :4000), so end-to-end tool-call validity via this server is unmeasured [uncertain].
context_and_limits: Live probe (/v1/models): id 'bielik', owned_by llamacpp, n_params 11168796672 (11.17B), size 9163218944 B (Q6_K, ~8.53 GiB), n_vocab 32128, n_embd 4096, n_ctx_train 32768. Runtime context: --ctx-size 16384 total with --parallel 2 -> 8192 ctx per slot (probe reports n_ctx 8192). Context strategy for omp: register with contextWindow 8192, not 32768 — the trained max is irrelevant at runtime with parallel 2.
model_registration: Recommended omp registration: model id 'nexgate/bielik' via LiteLLM :4000 (route already exists in the rendered template), api_base NEXGATE_BIELIK_API_BASE, supportsTools true, contextWindow 8192. Direct registration against http://127.0.0.1:8082/v1 (or https://mac-studio-jakub.tail5d39b4.ts.net:8082) with the same contextWindow also works for bypass setups. The <1s latency claim is user-reported for this server (prompt processing on empty-ish prompts); generation is the bottleneck, not first token [uncertain].
flags_and_budget: Launcher (cluster-migration/scripts/llama-bielik-vaultguard.sh): llama-server --model $LLAMA_CACHE_DIR/speakleash_Bielik-11B-v3.0-Instruct-Q6_K.gguf --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${BIELIK_SERVER_PORT:-8082} --alias bielik --ctx-size ${BIELIK_CONTEXT_LENGTH:-16384} -b 2048 -ub 2048 -fa on -ngl 99 -t 8 --mlock --prio 3 --parallel 2; logs to sovereign-agent-setup/logs/bielik-server.log. launchd com.jakub.llama-bielik: KeepAlive PathState on the GGUF volume path, RunAtLoad false, ThrottleInterval 30 — server starts when /Volumes/models mounts and stays up. .env: BIELIK_REPO=bartowski/speakleash_Bielik-11B-v3.0-Instruct-GGUF, BIELIK_MODEL_FILE=speakleash_Bielik-11B-v3.0-Instruct-Q6_K.gguf, BIELIK_SERVER_HOST=mac-studio-jakub.tail5d39b4.ts.net, BIELIK_SERVER_PORT=8082, BIELIK_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384, BIELIK_LAUNCHD_MANAGED=1, LLAMA_CACHE_DIR=/Volumes/models/llama.cpp. Memory: ~11 GB RSS with mlock; plan headroom around co-tenants.
litellm_route: Template litellm.yaml.tmpl (bielik block): model_name 'bielik', model 'openai/bielik', api_base from NEXGATE_BIELIK_API_BASE env, api_key sk-noop, drop_params true, additional_drop_params [web_search_options], region_name eu, model_info context_window 16384 with supports_function_calling/tool_choice/parallel_function_calling true, disable_background_health_check true. Fallbacks: allowed bielik -> [scaleway-devstral, mistral]; context_window_fallbacks for bielik: []. Member of SIMPLE model group. Note: template declares context_window 16384 but the serving reality per slot is 8192 (parallel 2) — either set --parallel 1 for full 16384 per request or correct the route's context_window to 8192 to avoid silent truncation [uncertain]. Rendered runtime yaml is REGENERATED by scripts/render-litellm-config.py — edit the template, then re-render, never hand-edit runtime/state/litellm.yaml.
backend_serving: llama-server from sovereign-agent-setup/llama.cpp build on Mac Studio (Apple silicon, -ngl 99 full offload, -fa on, --mlock, --prio 3, 8 threads). Throughput measured live from server log under concurrent 2-slot load: ~10.5-12.7 t/s per slot (tg_3s dipping to ~7.3-8 during contention). For omp coding turns (1-3k output tokens) expect ~1.5-5 min per response at this rate — far above cloud-API speeds; TASK_TIMEOUT-style budgets must account for it. DFlash speculative decoding: the llama.cpp checkout contains full DFLASH arch support (draft+verify, requires 'target_layers' GGUF metadata) and a matching ~1.17B draft model exists (speakleash Bielik-11B-v3.0-DFlash), but the launcher passes no --model-draft, so speculative decode is OFF [uncertain whether GGUF carries target_layers].
tool_call_rate: Not measured against this server: neither the omp suite nor the 20-call curl gate targeted :8082 (both hit coopforge via NexGate :4000). Native-template <tool_call> emission for get_time-style probes is expected to mirror the 100% curl-gate result given the same template family, but this is inference, not measurement [uncertain]. Running bielik-gateway-test.sh with api_base pointed at http://127.0.0.1:8082/v1 would close this gap.
streaming_behavior: llama-server streams SSE per OpenAI spec (--parallel slots stream independently); no dedicated streaming gate was run. Log shows steady per-slot decode cadence under concurrency with tg_3s variance (~7.3-12.7 t/s) when co-tenants contend. First-token latency: <1s reported for light prompts [uncertain — user-reported, not instrumented]; prompt-processing cost grows with tool-schema-laden system prompts (6-tool omp schema ~ hundreds of tokens) and 8192-slot KV occupancy.
reasoning_core_gate: Bielik v3 template supports a thinking mode (enable_thinking -> <think>...</think> blocks with Polish-language reasoning instructions embedded in the template). The served GGUF's default thinking behavior and whether reasoning content is stripped before tool parsing were not tested [uncertain]. No reasoning-core gate ran against :8082; gate results for the coopforge route live in reasoning_core_gate_omp.json.
pass_criteria: For this server to count as the local Bielik backend for omp: (1) /v1/models reachable — VERIFIED live (id bielik, 11.17B Q6_K). (2) Tool round-trip via /v1/chat/completions with tools + native template — NOT YET VERIFIED against :8082 [uncertain]. (3) Throughput compatible with task budgets — ~10.5-12.7 t/s/slot measured; adequate only with generous timeouts (300s ~ 3k tokens worst case). (4) Route registered in LiteLLM with correct context_window (8192 per slot) and SIMPLE-group membership — template exists, value mismatch flagged. (5) Survival under co-tenant load — Mac Studio runs claimkb mirror and other services pushing load to 150-240 with 26-37 GB swap; bielik walls will stretch under that pressure. Overall: serving infra solid; tool-call verification and route context_window fix are the two open items.
